name: CR-Diff-06-chain-1.b
generalfeedback:
In order to solve this problem we will have to use the chain rule <hint>calc_chain_rule</hint> as follows:

Define \(f({{CT:2}})={{CT:3}}\) and \(g({{CT:2}})={{CT:4}}\).

So \(f({{CT:2}})=g({{CT:2}})^{{CT:5}}\). So,

\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle
  \frac{d}{d{{CT:2}}}[{{CT:3}}] &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  \frac{df}{dg}\cdot \frac{dg}{d{{CT:2}}} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  \frac{d}{dg}(g^{{CT:5}})\cdot \frac{d}{d{{CT:2}}}({{CT:4}}) \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:5}}g^{{{CT:5}}-1}\cdot (-{{CT:6}}){{CT:2}}^{{{CT:6}}-1} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  -{{CT:7}}{{CT:2}}^{{CT:8}}({{CT:4}})^{{CT:9}} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  -{{CT:10}}
 \end{array}\]
